translations.text: Because of this, my grain
Now I will expose her filth before her lovers, and no one will be able to rescue her from my hand.
And I will take away all her joy, her festivals, her new moons, her Sabbaths, and all her great festivals.
And I will destroy her vines and her fig trees.
Therefore, look, I will lead her astray, and
there, as in the days of her youth and as in the days when she came up from Egypt.
And on that day, says the Lord, she will call me “My husband,” and from now on she will no longer call me “Baalim.”
And I will remove the names of the Baals from her mouth, so that she will not remember their names.

And on that day I will make a covenant for them with the wild animals of the field, the birds of the sky, and the creeping creatures of the earth. I will destroy the bow, the sword, and war from the earth, and I will make her live on the land in hope.
And I will betroth you to myself forever. I will betroth you in righteousness and justice, in mercy and compassion.
And I will betroth you to myself in faithfulness, and you will know the Lord.
And on that day, says the Lord, I will respond to the earth.
And the earth will respond to the grain, the wine, and the oil, and they will respond to [?].
And I will sow her for myself on the earth, and I will love the one who was not loved. I will say to the one who is not my people, ‘You are my people,’ and he will say, ‘You are the Lord my God.’
The Lord said to me, ‘Go again and love a woman who loves evil things and is an adulteress, just as God loves the children of Israel, although they look to foreign gods and eat raisin cakes.’
And I went and hired her for myself for fifteen pieces of silver, a measure of barley, and a measure of wine.
And I said to her, ‘Stay with me for many days. Do not prostitute yourself or belong to another husband. I too will be yours.’
For the children of [?] will remain for many days without [?].
And afterward the children of Israel will return and seek the Lord their God and David their king. They will stand in awe of the Lord and his good things in the last days.
Listen to the word of the Lord, children of [?], because the Lord has a case against those who live on the earth, for there is no truth on the earth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God.
Cursing has spread over the earth, along with lying, murder, theft, and adultery, and they will shed blood upon blood.
Therefore the earth will mourn, and all who live on the earth will dwindle, along with the wild animals of the field and the birds of the sky. The fish of the sea will also perish.
So let no one judge, and let no one rebuke anyone. And the people will be like a priest who is contradicted.
He will grow weak during the day, and the prophet too will grow weak with him. I have compared your mother to the night.

My people have become like someone who has no knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I too will reject you, so that you cannot serve me. And because you have forgotten the law of your God, I too will forget your children.
In proportion, this is how they sinned against me. I will turn their glory into shame.
They will eat the sins of my people, and they will take their souls in their acts of injustice.
And the priest will become like the people. I will punish him for his lawless deeds, and I will repay him for the thoughts of his heart.
They will eat but will not be satisfied. They have prostituted themselves, but they will not prosper, because they have abandoned the Lord, to keep watch.
[?] sexual immorality, and the people's heart took in wine and drunkenness.
He consulted his wood, and they answered him through their rods, because they were led astray by a spirit of sexual immorality. They committed sexual immorality and abandoned God.

They offered sacrifices on the mountain peaks and burned incense on the hills, under an oak, a poplar, and a shade tree, because its shade is good. Therefore your daughters will commit sexual immorality, and your daughters-in-law will commit adultery.

And I will not punish your daughters when they commit sexual immorality, or your daughters-in-law when they commit adultery, because they themselves associated with prostitutes and offered incense to those who are defiled. And the people who have understanding stumbled into a prostitute.
But you, Israel, do not be ignorant. And Judah, do not enter Gilgal or go up to the house of injustice, and do not swear by the living Lord.
For like a stubborn heifer, so [?] was stubborn. Now the Lord will pasture them like a lamb in a wide-open place.
Ephraim associated himself with idols; he set stumbling blocks before himself.
He rivaled the Canaanites in prostitution. They prostituted themselves because of me; they loved disgrace because of his pride.
A wind will cry out with its wings, and they will be ashamed because of their altars.
Listen to these things, priests, and
blow a trumpet on the hills, cry out on the high places, and proclaim in the house of On that Benjamin is dismayed.
And Ephraim went to the Assyrians and sent messengers to King Arim. But he could not heal you, nor will he give you relief, and your pains will not leave you.
For I am like a panther to Ephraim and like a lion to the house of Judah. I will seize and go away; I will carry off, and there is no one who will rescue from my hand.
I will go and return to my place until I [?], and they will seek my face.
In their distress they will come to me early, saying, “Come, let us return to the Lord our God, because he is the one who struck us, and he will heal us. He will wound us, and he will treat us.
He will save us after two days, and on the third day we will rise and know him.
And we will hurry to know the Lord. We will find him ready like the dawn, and he will come like rain upon the earth, early and late.”
Knowledge of God more than burnt offerings.
But they are like a person who breaks a covenant. There she acted unfaithfully toward me—
Gilead, the city that does worthless things. Its footprint
is made of blood, and your strength is like that of a robber. The priests concealed the Lord's way; they murdered in Shechem and committed lawlessness.
In the [?]
Woe to them, because they fled from me! Misery will overtake them, because they acted wickedly against me. I redeemed them, but they spoke lies against me.
And they did not cry out to me in their hearts; they wailed on their beds.
I instructed them, but they turned away from me and plotted evil against me.
They turned to worthless things and became like a bent bow. Their rulers will fall by the sword because of the ignorance of their tongue.
I will bring disgrace and anguish on them because they have broken my covenant and disregarded my law.
They will cry out to me, “God, we know you! Do not cast us away from you.”
Their hearts are divided. Now they will perish. He himself will tear down their altars, and their pillars will be brought low.
For now they will say, “We have no king because we did not fear the Lord. And what can the king do for us?”
[?] he will speak deceitful, lying words. He will establish a covenant, and judgment will spring up like a weed in a field left fallow.

Because of the calf of Beth-aven, the inhabitants of Samaria will become strangers. Its people mourned over it, and just as they exalted it, they will rejoice over its glory, because they have carried it away from it.
And after they bound it, they took it to the Assyrians as a gift for King Jareb. Ephraim will receive it with honor. [?] will be ashamed of his counsel.
Samaria has cast away its king like a piece of wood on the surface of the water.
And they will remove the high places of injustice there, the sins of [?]. Thorns and thistles will grow over their altars. They will say to the mountains, “Cover us,” and to the hills, “Fall on us.”
Since the hills stood, [?] sinned in that place. He will not overtake them on the hill. There is a war against the children of injustice
when they act unjustly. And I will discipline them. Peoples will gather against them when they are disciplined for their two acts of injustice. Up to this point.
God, who is in you, will have mercy on an orphan.
I will heal their dwelling places, and I will have mercy on these. I will turn my anger away from them, and
I will be like a father to [?], and he will blossom like, like a lily. He will put down roots like Lebanon.
His branches will spread out, and they will be like an olive tree bearing its fruit. His fragrance will be like Lebanon.
They will return and sit beneath his shade. They will live and satisfy themselves with grain. They will blossom like a grapevine.
